artifacts.summary: Fixed the quoted-case-pattern /** containment bug at both is_contained_v10 (git-commit-scoped.sh) and its ported twin (git-commit-phase.sh), added six deep-glob test cases across both suites (all observed RED against pre-fix behaviour), and redeployed the source store.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed the quoted-entry-disables-own-glob bug in both is_contained_v10 (git-commit-scoped.sh) and its ported twin is_contained (git-commit-phase.sh), so a /**-suffixed file_scope entry now contains its direct children and every deeper descendant without widening containment for any non-/** entry or same-prefix sibling. Added Z11-Z14 and Case 10-11 test coverage (each independently confirmed RED against pre-fix behaviour), redeployed via deploy-headless.sh, and confirmed both deployed copies carry the fix via a live sanity check against a real /** entry in specs/state.json.

memory_candidates.content: Shell containment/matching predicates that do `case "$path" in "$entry"/*)` with a QUOTED variable never glob-expand asterisks the variable's OWN value carries -- quoting disables glob interpretation of the pattern, so an entry like `foo/**` becomes the literal two-asterisk string, matching almost nothing. The fix is NOT to unquote (which would let an attacker/task-authored string inject arbitrary glob syntax) -- it is to detect the specific suffix you want to treat specially (e.g. a literal trailing `/**`) via parameter expansion (`${entry%/\*\*}`), and branch explicitly when it was present. Audit any case-pattern matcher that takes a data-sourced (not hardcoded) pattern string for this exact footgun.

A write-time PreToolUse hook that validates an Edit/Write call (e.g. validate-no-task-references.sh) typically receives only that call's own new_string/content as input, NOT the full file. A file-wide exemption marker (task-ref-ok:begin/:end) placed far above the edited region in a PRIOR edit is invisible to a hook scanning only the CURRENT call's new_string. When adding new content containing an otherwise-exempt pattern (e.g. synthetic '--task 999' test fixture literals) to a file that already has such markers elsewhere, wrap the NEW block in its OWN nested begin/end pair rather than assuming the file's existing far-away markers cover it.

When writing a test case to prove a path-containment predicate's new behaviour (e.g. a /** deep-glob branch), do not place the test fixture under a directory that a test harness's OWN implicit/default scope-widening already admits unconditionally (e.g. a fixture task's own task-directory member). That widening will make the case pass regardless of whether the predicate change under test is correct, silently proving nothing. Choose a base path that sits entirely outside every implicit scope member so a passing case is attributable only to the change being tested.
